page: Microsoft Azure M208s_v2 is an x86_64 architecture server instance belonging to the MSv2 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features dedicated CPU allocation powered by Intel Xeon 8280L processors, providing 208 vCPUs across 104 physical cores with 2 threads per core at a clock speed of 2.7 GHz. The memory configuration is exceptionally large, offering 2850.0 GB of RAM, which translates to 13.7 GB per core. The instance includes 4194 GB of local storage and is Premium Storage capable, though it does not include any GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data reveals a stark contrast between single-core and multi-core performance. Single-threaded operations, such as stress-ng single-core CPU performance, gzip compression, and bzip3 decompression, fall into the bottom 25% tier. Conversely, multi-threaded capabilities are highly performant, with stress-ng multi-core CPU performance, bzip3 multi-threaded decompression, and PassMark CPU extended instructions scoring in the top 10%. Memory bandwidth is also highly efficient, with cached small-block read speeds reaching 10456.14 GB/sec and uncached large-block write speeds at 191.08 GB/sec, both ranking in the top 10%. Redis SET operations also perform in the top tier, achieving 153.96 million operations per second.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the M208s_v2 represents a high-density resource profile designed for enterprise-scale workloads where massive memory capacity and multi-core parallelization justify the infrastructure class. The instance is highly suited for large-scale in-memory databases, heavy multi-threaded data processing, and enterprise database operations. However, it is less optimal for workloads dependent on high single-core clock speeds or real-time LLM text generation on medium-to-large models, where its single-threaded performance and lack of GPU acceleration present clear bottlenecks.
